TextAnalysis.title: TextAnalysis
TextAnalysis.description: Represents a record of an AI-powered textual analysis of animal food descriptions or symptoms.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TextAnalysis entity.

userId.description: Reference to the user who performed this analysis. (Relationship: User 1:N TextAnalysis)

inputText.description: The textual description provided by the user for analysis (e.g., food ingredients, animal symptoms).

aiResponse.description: The detailed analysis, insights, and recommendations generated by the AI based on the input text.

analysisDate.description: The timestamp indicating when the textual analysis was performed.

language.description: The language in which the analysis was performed and the AI response was generated (e.g., 'pt-BR').

ImageAnalysis.title: ImageAnalysis
ImageAnalysis.description: Represents a record of an AI-powered image analysis of animal food labels, food items, or animal symptoms.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ImageAnalysis entity.

userId.description: Reference to the user who performed this analysis. (Relationship: User 1:N ImageAnalysis)

imageUrl.description: The URL or path to the image uploaded or captured by the user for analysis.

imageDescription.description: An optional textual description provided by the user to give context to the image (e.g., 'rótulo da ração X', 'sintoma na pata direita').

aiResponse.description: The detailed analysis, insights, and recommendations generated by the AI based on the input image.

analysisDate.description: The timestamp indicating when the image analysis was performed.

language.description: The language in which the analysis was performed and the AI response was generated (e.g., 'pt-BR').

definition.description: Stores individual AI-powered textual analyses performed by a user. Each document is owned by the user specified in the path and includes the 'userId' field for explicit ownership and authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who performed this textual analysis.

params.name: textAnalysisId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific textual analysis.

definition.description: Stores individual AI-powered image analyses performed by a user. Each document is owned by the user specified in the path and includes the 'userId' field for explicit ownership and authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who performed this image analysis.

params.name: imageAnalysisId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific image analysis.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be highly secure, scalable, and debuggable, strictly adhering to the core design principles. Both 'TextAnalysis' and 'ImageAnalysis' entities are modeled as subcollections under individual user documents. This 'Path-Based Ownership' approach leverages the natural hierarchical nature of Firestore.

**Authorization Independence:** This structure inherently achieves authorization independence. By placing `TextAnalysis` documents under `/users/{userId}/textAnalyses/{textAnalysisId}` and `ImageAnalysis` documents under `/users/{userId}/imageAnalyses/{imageAnalysisId}`, the `userId` in the path directly identifies the owner. Firestore security rules can then easily compare `request.auth.uid` with the `{userId}` wildcard in the path. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls to parent user documents to ascertain ownership or permissions, as the ownership is self-evident from the document's location. Furthermore, the `userId` field is explicitly included in both `TextAnalysis` and `ImageAnalysis` schemas. While the path itself provides sufficient authorization context, this internal `userId` field acts as a denormalized ownership indicator within the document, reinforcing authorization independence and simplifying future rule logic or data migrations.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** This design strongly supports Query-As-Permissions. Since each user's analyses are stored in their dedicated subcollection (e.g., `/users/{request.auth.uid}/textAnalyses`), a user can only list, get, create, update, or delete documents within their own scope. There is no central, global collection of analyses that would require complex server-side filtering (which is not how Firestore security rules operate for `list` queries). A `list` operation performed by `request.auth.uid` on `/users/{request.auth.uid}/textAnalyses` will only ever return documents owned by that user, making the `list` operation inherently secure and compliant with QAPs.
